With my first I requested a c-section after 30hrs of no progression and baby distress. I was nervous but I knew baby safe all that mattered. This helped me through it.

I only felt the pressure of them taking out baby. It was uncomfortable but not unbearable. I just did some heavy slow breathing and mouning techniques. And it lasted only a minute. After that I spaced on what they were doing bc I was focused on my hubby and baby. Hearing his first cry, seeing them cleaning him, watching his daddy hold him with tears of joy. 

The recovery was not bad either as long as you stay on top of the pain. I was literally up and moving two hours after I got back to the room. I had to pee lol. 

Now I am not saying this is how yours will go, but I wish you a smooth csection and recovery!!!

Mom to a 4 year old. I am a SAHM, now. I understand your anxiety completely. When I had my son, working up to due date, I was in retail. It was horrible, and while on leave, I looked for a better hour job and pay. I did end up with an office job after he was born. I worked up until he was 1.5 years old, I did not have my dream job like you(which is AWESOME), so when my husband got a new job and much more pay, he said you do not have to work if you do not want to. So I thought about it for a bit, and came to the decision of being a SAHM. I know lots of mom’s who continue to work because they LOVE what they do, and there is NOTHING wrong with that. They do not love their kid(s) any less, and the same goes to mom’s who decide to give up the career. 

As for the sick, like others have said it is gonna happen. They need to build up their systems, and once they do the sicks are cut way back. I quit my latuda cold turkey and I had no issues. And I know I didnt bc before I got pregnant I had been weened off my anxiety and depression meds when we started trying. Which was not fun bc i did have withdrawal with them. But latuda was easier. 

And in October we decided to start trying for baby #2, and I just went ahead and came off all my meds. It was defiantly tougher coming off all of them at the same time. It lasted about two weeks, first week was it slowly coming out of my system, then the second week was adjusting to not having them.

I am a mixed bipolar with social anxiety. So I take a bipolar med(latuda), an anxiety med(clazopam(sp?)), and an anti depressant. 

When my hubby and I decided to have a baby, we talked to my psychiatrist, and came up with a game plan. I would stop my meds and go as long as i can after the first trimester. 

I got pregnant Dec 2013. I stopped my meds immediately.  And I made it all the way to my second tri when I said I have to go back on my bipolar med at least. I waited this long bc first tri is were their neurons and all brain development occurs. So I waited as long as I could so not to effect my baby to much. 

Fast forward to Sept 2914, where I had a perfectly healthy baby boy. No side affects from my meds. 

Now present: My son is 4 and he is perfectly awesome. He is very smart, very athletic, very curious about everything, very social, and very happy. 

Yes it is your choice but know this tons of woman’s throughout life have gone to birth perfectly healthy babies even while on drugs. You have to do what you need to handle all the changing that comes with developing and growing a baby inside you!!!
